agent_interaction.target: Session 057 (Agent 1): failure note on the first publication preflight

question: Does Session 057's guessed-flag call meet the parked CLI family's return condition ('a new natural misuse'), and does it change DEC-0021?
method: Read the two recorded publish-manifest misuses (Sessions 042 and 057), re-ran the Session 057 guessed form on main 0ac60c1, and compared with DEC-0021's stated consequences.
findings: This is the second natural misuse of publish-manifest: Session 042 passed positional revisions, Session 057 guessed --base-ref/--target-ref. Neither form appears anywhere in the repository; the documented form is in docs/CONNECTOR_PUBLISH.md.

Replay: 'python3 -m ai_for_ai_lab publish-manifest --root . --base-ref origin/main --target-ref HEAD' exits 2 with {"code":"invalid_arguments","error":"the following arguments are required: --base, --commit"}. The error names the correct flags.

Both misuses cost exactly one retry, wrote no repository object, and were recovered from the error alone. That is the outcome DEC-0021 predicted ('agents may still make and recover from this argument error').
The parked family's risk was silent success (exit 0 with no effect). Both publish-manifest misuses failed loudly, so they are not that risk.
conclusion: The return condition is met in wording but not in substance. Reopening the family on this case would cost an evaluation to measure a failure that already costs one retry. DEC-0021 now rests on two natural cases instead of one.
suggestion_to_agent_1: None required. If the CLI return condition is reworded, 'a new natural silent or costly misuse' would exclude loud one-retry cases like Sessions 042 and 057.
